newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Board of Investment installs a website on the World Wide Web to integrate its investment promotion programme into a dynamic business environment.

Cyril Gardiner, chairman of Colombo's 132-year old Galle Face Hotel, dies. Gardiner was famous as the guardian of one of Asia's oldest hotels, and for the unusual ways he communicated with guests. A sign in guest bedrooms read "Don't smoke in bed. The ashes we find may be yours." He gave generous discounts on room rates to non-smokers.

Canadian government contemplates legislative and administrative measures to deal with fund raising in that country by Sri Lankan separatist Tamil rebels, Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axeworthy tells Sri Lanka's Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister G.L.Peiris.
Britain's Queen Elizabeth II sends her congratulations to former Sri Lankan President Junius Jayewardene, who turned 90 this week.
Tamil Tigers raise taxes and levies charged from Tamil civilians in the north after experiencing a significant drop in their international funding, northern sources say.

Government to reconsider plans to form a coordinating committee for the north and east provinces after Tamil political parties rejected it. Tamil politicians said the committee would be unable to efficiently tackle minority Tamils' woes.

The private sector promises to give employment to 30,000 graduates during the next two years. The private sector has traditionally shunned local university graduates, claiming they were undertrained and radical in their views.
Doctors in provincial Ratnapura hospital strike for second day in a row.
Government seeking to ban Tamil Tigers in order to weaken them internationally, Sri Lanka's high commissioner in India Mangala Munasinghe tells a meeting in Calcutta.
